awd_titl_txt: Travel: NSF Student Travel Grant for 2025 IEEE International Midwest  Symposium of Circuits and Systems (MWSCAS25)
awd_abstract_narration:
This award supports student travel for attending undergraduate and graduate students to the 65th (International) Midwest Symposium on Circuits and Systems (MWCAS), sponsored by the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE), to be hosted in Lansing, Michigan, USA on Aug. 10-13, 2025. The MWCAS is a premier international conference in the field of circuits and systems. Other than tutorials, keynote, and plenary lectures by leading experts in the field, the conference will be attended by academic and industry researchers and students to present their recent work both in lecture sessions and poster sessions. The conference will host a student paper competition to encourage the best students to keep abreast of the most modern technologies. Recipients of this travel grant will be selected from the pool of students presenting papers and will be paid part of their expenses for travel and registration at the conference. US citizens and permanent residents will be given the highest priority in the selection process. The experience gained by the students in the process is going to be an invaluable component of their education. Due to a good number of industrial participants in the meeting, the experience will also help the students to secure positions in industry, thus contributing to the much-needed technological workforce of the United States. Education and Work Force Development for microelectronics is a major focus of MWCAS 2025. 

The conference will extensively cover technical areas in Circuits and Systems, including, but not limited to: Analog and Mixed Signal Circuits and Systems, Digital Integrated Circuits and Systems, Power and Energy Circuits and Systems, Sensory Circuits and Systems, Signal, Image, and Multimedia Processing, Communications Circuits and Systems, Radio Frequency (RF) and Wireless Circuits and Systems, Biomedical Circuits and Systems, Neural Networks and Neuromorphic Engineering, Beyond CMOS Circuits and Architectures.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

Travel: NSF Student Travel Grant for 2025 IEEE International Midwest Symposium of Circuits and Systems (MWSCAS25) 

Project Outcomes Report

The NSF Student Participation Grant supported student attendance at the 2025 IEEE 68th International Midwest Symposium on Circuits and Systems (MWSCAS 2025), held in Lansing, Michigan, from August 10-13, 2025. MWSCAS is one of the leading international conferences in circuits and systems, bringing together researchers, engineers, industry professionals, and students working in areas such as microelectronics, integrated circuits, sensing technologies, communications, artificial intelligence hardware, and emerging computing systems.

A total of 255 participants attended the conference, including 61 students. NSF support enabled 33 students from universities across the United States to participate who otherwise may have faced financial barriers to attendance. The conference theme, Designing a Smart Autonomous Tomorrow, reflected the growing role of intelligent sensing, edge computing, and autonomous systems in modern circuits and systems research.

The conference featured peer-reviewed presentations, tutorials, special sessions, student demonstrations, and networking activities spanning integrated circuits, sensing systems, communications, biomedical electronics, power systems, and emerging AI-enabled hardware.

Students presented research papers, attended tutorials and technical sessions, met researchers from academia and industry, and participated in networking and mentoring activities throughout the conference. These activities allowed students to exchange technical ideas, receive feedback on ongoing research, and learn about current developments across the circuits and systems community.

A major student-focused activity was the MWSCAS Student-Industry Forum, where students discussed career paths, workforce needs, and emerging technologies with engineers and technical leaders from industry. The forum enabled direct interaction with professionals working in microelectronics, sensing systems, communications, autonomous technologies, and AI-enabled hardware.

Student feedback consistently cited three benefits: exposure to research outside their immediate area, direct interaction with researchers and industry representatives, and the opportunity to present and discuss their work with a broader technical audience. Many students also reported that the conference helped them identify new research directions, establish professional connections, and gain a better understanding of potential academic and industrial career pathways.

NSF support enabled students from a broad range of U.S. universities to participate in a major international technical conference and engage directly with the circuits and systems research community. The experience helped students communicate their research, develop professional connections, and gain exposure to current advances in microelectronics, sensing, communications, and AI-enabled systems.
